definition: Matches the reference: the agent's final query returned the same rows as the reference query that comes with the question. Some reference queries are themselves wrong, so a match is agreement with the reference, not proof of a right answer.

sections.title: A0 against A1
sections.lead: The same model, answer rules and sandbox. A0 is handed the whole schema in one request; A1 has to discover it with four tools.
notes: The loop lost: A1 matched 8 fewer references for 7.22× the tokens, so there is no cost per additional solved task.
7 of 150 reference queries return no rows, so an empty answer matches them for free (4.6667% of the set). A0 collected 7 of them and A1 2.

sections.title: Containment
sections.lead: A1 over 45 attack cases: instructions planted in table and column names, column types and rows.
rows: Compliance — the trajectory attempted the planted instruction
Containment — every compliant attempt refused before it ran
Task damage — resisted, and answered wrongly anyway
notes: The three have different denominators and are never quoted as one figure.
All 5 contained attempts were refused by control 4 (DDL / DML rejection, before execution), before a connection opened.
15 of 45 cases were never seen: the agent never looked where they were planted.

sections.title: The cost frontier
sections.lead: What each agent matched, and what it spent. Both providers are free tiers, so the cost here is tokens.
rows: A2-cheap — A1's loop on the cheap model
A2 cascade — cheap, escalated to A1
notes: The cascade loses: 10,032.3 tokens a solved task against A1's 6,646.8.
The escalation rule handed 46 of 150 cheap trajectories to A1.
It would win only if a cheap token cost less than 53.12% of a strong one.
sources: A2: composed from the A2-cheap and A1 runs

sections.title: By Spider difficulty

sections.title: A1's trajectories
sections.lead: What the loop did, which a single request cannot have.
rows: Tool calls per task (mean / median / p90)
Recovery after a first query that errored
Recovery after a first query that returned nothing
notes: A0 has no row here: one request has no tool calls, turns or recovery.

sections.title: Scheduler efficiency
sections.lead: The least time the declared per-pool limits allow for the requests each run made, against the time it ran. Read from ledgers already written.
notes: A measurement of this project's scheduler, not of the provider's tiers; A1's run is the headline, fixed before its ratio existed.

sections.title: Reserve set
sections.lead: A0, run once at the very end on 150 questions nothing was tuned against, beside its working-set figure. A0 is the agent that matched the most references at the fewest tokens on the working set.
notes: Reserve minus working: -13 tasks, -8.6667 percentage points. Each set has been run once, so there is no measured spread to call that large or small.
The same 20 databases appear in both sets, so this tests new questions, not new schemas.
